chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Yusuf ibn al-Harith, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Arzmī, from his father Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon him), who said:

Umar was brought a man who had been sodomized in his backside, so he intended to whip him. He said to the witnesses, 'Did you see him entering it as the reed is inserted into the kohl container?' They said, 'Yes.' He said to Ali (peace be upon him), 'What do you view regarding this?' So he sought the stallion that had copulated with him but did not find him. Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'I view that his neck should be struck.'

He said, 'So he ordered for his neck to be struck off. Then he said, 'Hold him, for there remains for him another punishment.' They said, 'And what is it?' He said, 'Call for a tun of firewood!' So he called for a tun of firewood. So he (the body) was wrapped in it, then brought out and incinerated with the fire.

He said, 'Then he said: Allah has servants for whom in their loins are wombs like the wombs of women.' He said, 'So why do they not become pregnant in them?' He said, 'Because it is inverted in their backsides, a gland like the gland of the camel. So when it stirs, they stir, and when it is calm, they are calm.'

key_terms.الْمِيلُ: reed (used as a metaphor for the penis)

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd punishment for sodomy according to Ali ibn Abi Talib in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the juristic evolution of *Liwan* (sodomy) penalties, contrasting Umar’s initial hesitation with Ali’s definitive ruling of neck-beating (*Darb al-Raqaba*) in the absence of the animal partner, followed by incineration of the body. It further provides a unique physiological explanation for male pregnancy, attributing it to an inverted gland (*ghudda*) in the loins, reflecting the intersection of fiqh and early medical understanding in Shia scholarship.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Yusuf Bin Al Haris, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Rahman A lArzamy, from his father Abdul Rahman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘They came to Umar with a man who had been sodomised in his backside. So he understood that he should be whipped. So he said to the witnesses, ‘Did you all see him to be entered into like the entering of the applicator into the kohl?’ So they said, ‘Yes’. So he said to Ali<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What do you<sup>asws</sup> view with regards to this?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> sought the stallion who had copulated with him, but he was not found. So Ali<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> see with regards to him that you should strike his neck’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So he ordered for his neck to be struck off. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Hold him, for there remains for him another punishment’. They said, ‘And what is it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Call for some firewood!’ So he called for some firewood. So he (the body) was wrapped, then brought out and incinerated with the fire.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has servants, for whom in their loins are wombs like the wombs of the women’. He said, ‘So what is for them that they do not become pregnant in these?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because it is inverted in their backsides, a gland like the gland of the camel. So when it stirs, they stir, and when it is calm, they are calm’.
